newsitem.title: UK: Minor metals - Bismuth moves higher, cadmium probes.
newsitem.headline: Minor metals - Bismuth moves higher, cadmium probes.

text.p: Trade covering against the backdrop of falling stocks saw bismuth climb higher in minor metals trading over the past week, while cadmium was also starting to probe upside territory, traders said.
Short supply and talk that major producer China may be holding back some available stock saw bismuth trading above $3.00 a pound.
Low Peruvian/Mexican stocks, trade and a hint of speculative buying, could see the market move higher over the coming weeks, traders said.
"There is a lot of interest emerging in the market against a backdrop of falling stocks and improving fundamentals," one commented.

A small five cent tick higher in cadmium could signal a start of a run up in prices as sellers look to take advantage of anticipated covering of a large short position. Traders said prices could move towards $1 a pound near-term.

A conference in Hong Kong by the Cobalt Development Institute (CDI) saw European trading business for the metal slow, though one London based trader attending the meeting said near-term cobalt had the potential to register substantial gains.
"There has been a lot of enquiry to buy cobalt in its high grade form given the booming demand from the aerospace industry," he said.
Offtake for the metal in the battery industry and a backdrop of Zambia hitting low ore bodies were supportive. Japanese consumers were also believed to be covering.
European traders noted several news items from the Hong Kong meeting.
Peter Searle, head of UK-based Resource Strategies said that the world's cobalt supplies will remain healthy, regardless of whether Zaire develops its cobalt projects.
Japan's primary cobalt consumption in 1997 will jump to 6,500 tonnes from 5,700 tonnes last year, a Japanese industry official said on Thursday.
"In 1997, we anticipate 6,500 metric tonnes of primary cobalt consumption in Japan at present," Ryoichi Terada, assistant general manager of the cobalt section at Mitsui & Co Ltd.
The price of cobalt could increase up to $30 per pound within the next two or three months, a senior cobalt industry source said on Wednesday, a view shared by others present at the conference.
"The cobalt price, between now and the next two or three months could hit $30 per pound again," said Ed Kielty, head of U.S.-based Hall Chemical Company.
He said that the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency stockpile would continue to be an overhang factor, and that Zaire would continue to overshadow perceptions.
Action in the antimony market was slow but several traders suggested that shipments from China were arriving or were on the way to Rotterdam.
The recent rally in indium stalled as some profit-taking crept in, while molybdenum remained steady against the backdrop of enquiry from steelmills.
